headline: Proposed freeze on TIF and TIE tax incentives for developers failed in two votes.
summary: The freeze would have paused TIF and TIE decisions until a sliding-scale incentive package was created. A substitute motion would have waited 120 days first; it failed 2-8, and the original motion was then defeated. Speakers during public comment were split, with some warning the freeze could cost state money and stall projects. The council also approved a land disposition agreement with Cabot, Cabot & Forbes for Parcel A2 in the Hamilton Canal Innovation District, 8-2.

discussion: TIF and TIE freeze: Members and speakers debated whether a freeze would set clear standards or delay projects. The Lowell Housing Authority's executive director said a project there needs its paperwork in place around December 11th.

Merrimack Street minutes: The council voted to release executive session minutes before the November 24th presentation. Members said the city clerk is off the week of Thanksgiving, and some asked for more time to review the minutes.
Gas pipe repairs: A speaker said the city's response did not include the utility's analysis of why it chose replacement over repair. The response was sent to the Technology Subcommittee.
City Council rules: Members said the proposed rule changes need more review. A speaker asked how the proposed consent agenda would affect public comment.
Parcel A2 maintenance: A councilor asked whether maintenance of the Utopia and Swan Block sites would continue after the deed is accepted. The solicitor said it would.
